item.title: SCP-5479:
item.content:encoded:
I don't hate this conceptually; but the actual execution feels far too reliant on shock horror to work for me. Like, the first couple of logs worked for me because they're kinda…weird without being over the top; but everything else feels like it's just too much.

There's a part of me that feels like this would be more interesting as an exploration of what counts as an enclosed space, with the finale being some entry where something that shouldn't be enclosed is and leaving us with a horrifying implication; but instead there's just…ever escalating shock.

item.title: The Shadow Door: Awkward, abrupt changes
item.content:encoded: The transitions between "base reality" and "storybook reality" are too sudden and awkwardly placed. How does this boy survive being eaten by his bed-turned-monster mouth? How ans why does the father disappear after his son esscapes? And how can s favorite adventure tale that's existed for decades suddenly act anomolous, without developing s reputation as "the book you'd better not read to kids…especially not by reassuring the kids that it's only fiction"? (Shades of SCP-1241 here…)
